objective.name: bubble_server_windows.py
objective.purpose: Create and arrange a fixed set of macOS Terminal.app windows (API Server, Metro Bundler, iOS App, Android App, General, Testing) with predefined titles, colors, and screen positions for local dev. 'windows' means terminal windows/panes, NOT the Windows OS. No-arg behavior: runs the 'create' command (opens all windows); it does NOT launch any processes — the panes are empty shells for manual commands.
objective.side_effects: Opens ~6 Terminal.app windows/tabs with custom titles, RGB colors, and computed positions. Does not start any server/process. 'kill' closes every Terminal window matching the known titles.
objective.language_packages: stdlib only (argparse, subprocess) — no third-party packages
invoked_languages: JavaScript / JXA (osascript -l JavaScript, for NSScreen size)
host_requirements: macOS only — controls Terminal.app and Finder via AppleScript/osascript
An active display with detectable dimensions
invocation_methods: Single window by name/partial: python3 scripts/bubble_server_windows.py api

switches.effect: Override auto-detected screen size for headless/misdetected displays
Print detected screen dims and computed window bounds before acting

objective.explicit_env_checks: false — no checks for Terminal.app/osascript presence; relies on osascript errors. Screen detection falls back JXA→system_profiler→Finder, then exits 1 if all fail

subjective.usual_invocation: Run by the developer (Travis) once at the start of a local session to lay out terminal panes; a personal convenience tool, not part of any automated pipeline.
subjective.invocation_change_recommendation: Move from verb-positional form (create/resize/kill/show_boundaries) to switch form (--create/--resize/--kill or a single --action) for consistency with the other tools. The verb form is acceptable but inconsistent with the switch-driven house style (e.g. bench_sims).
subjective.linux_changes_needed: Effectively a full rewrite. Every effect goes through Terminal.app via osascript and screen size via NSScreen/JXA — none of which exist on Linux. A port would need a different backend entirely (tmux session+windows, or gnome-terminal/xterm + xdotool) and screen detection via xrandr/Wayland. Treat as macOS-only; do not port — provide a tmux-based equivalent if a container layout is ever needed.

macos_dependency.notes: Deeply macOS-bound: osascript, Terminal.app, Finder, NSScreen, system_profiler. Zero portability by design.

subjective.typical_runtime: A few seconds (synchronous AppleScript with built-in 0.3s delays per window).
subjective.dry_run_recommendation: Yes — a true --dry-run that prints the planned window titles/colors/bounds without opening or closing anything. --debug already prints computed bounds but still acts; promote it to a no-op preview.
subjective.destructive_steps: 'kill' closes every Terminal window whose title matches a known name — could close windows the user did not create with this tool if titles collide. It does not kill processes, but closing a window with a running server underneath effectively stops it.
subjective.rewrite_language_recommendation: Keep in Python on macOS. If cross-platform layout is ever required, rewrite the backend around tmux (shell or Python+libtmux) rather than extending the osascript approach.
subjective.merge_recommendation: Keep standalone. It is unrelated to the test runners and is a personal layout helper.
subjective.rename_recommendation: Yes — the name is misleading ('windows' reads as the OS). Rename to something like bubble_term_layout (and optionally drop .py). Clarify in help that it manages macOS Terminal panes.
subjective.relocate_recommendation: Yes — it is a personal, rarely-used convenience tool. Move to a scripts/dev/ or scripts/local/ subdir so it does not sit next to the core test infrastructure.
subjective.improvement_suggestions: URGENT: fix the parse-time SyntaxError on line 335 (`global screen_left, screen_top, scr.en_width, screen_height` — `scr.en_width` should be `screen_width`); the script does not run at all in its current state (verified via python3 -m py_compile). Then add explicit preflight checks (osascript present, running on macOS), make titles/colors/layout data-driven from a small config, and promote --debug to a real --dry-run.
subjective.requirements_check_completeness: all implicit — no explicit guard for macOS/Terminal.app/osascript; failures surface only as osascript errors or a silent exit 1 when screen detection fails.
subjective.external_dependency_breakdown: Scoring policy (v1.0): +1 per env var; +1 per non-standard / separately-installed program (xcrun/simctl, Android SDK tools, maestro, grpcurl, psql, gmtool, node/npm, lnav, etc.); programs shipped with macOS (ps, lsof, top, pgrep, sysctl, open, pbcopy, curl, osascript, system_profiler, git, grep/sed/awk) are NOT counted; +5 if a simulator/emulator is required on the primary path; +10 per large non-default app required (Xcode, Android Studio/SDK, Genymotion, Postgres, brew). Here: env 0 + programs 0 (osascript and system_profiler both ship with macOS) + sim 0 + apps 0 (Terminal.app is a default) = 0. (Down from 2 under v0.9.)
subjective.change_score_rationale: Weights (v1.0): Linux portability full-block +8 / partial +4 / portable 0; other dimensions +1 (or +2 where noted). Linux FULL block +8 (deeply osascript/Terminal.app/NSScreen-bound; needs a tmux or gnome-terminal rewrite). Invocation (verb->switch) +1. Missing --dry-run +1. Destructive title-matched window close +1. Gating all-implicit +2. Rename (misleading name) +1. Relocate (rarely-used personal tool) +1. Backend rewrite for portability +2. Known bug — parse-time SyntaxError line 335, script entirely non-functional (verified via py_compile) +3. Total 20. Highest of the set.
subjective.quality_score_rationale: Anchored rubric (v1.0), sub-scores sum to 100 — Error-handling/robustness /25: 5; Tests /20: 0 (no self-tests); Structure/clarity /20: 12; Documentation /15: 9; Portability + explicit requirement checks /20: 2. Total 28. CURRENTLY NON-FUNCTIONAL — a parse-time SyntaxError on line 335 (verified via py_compile) means it does not run at all, so robustness scores near zero regardless of the otherwise-tidy argparse/screen-detection design; plus all-implicit gating and zero portability.
